masks.reason: the castle-top tick clears g_keyState; in this run (1 of the 5 reference runs) DOSBox-X redrew the clue box without the key: its castle-top tick landed between a frame's Frame_Begin and its Screen_DrawOverlay, a sub-tick race of the original's loop. avi_fits.wave5: wave 5 (frame order): a short frame's picture now shows from the tick that changed it, a long one's (a scroll step: 6.5-7.5 PIT ticks) from the tick after; in the trunk-climb AVI recorded with r2/fl_climb the climb's sprite steps and scroll steps now both fall on the fitted time base (mean offsets -0.16 and 0.00 ticks; before -0.81 and +0.09). In the castle AVIs the end sequence's animation frames appear about as late after their ticks as the scroll steps (relative offsets: before +0.2, now -0.8 ticks in ega_r2_end_t2_nokey.avi, recorded with r2/fl_end_t2_wait, whose ticks the engine matches one for one): those frames (several large sprites drawn and presented) last about 6 PIT ticks on the reference machine, which no log measures yet (the FRAME ring of r2/fl_end_t2_wait holds only the rank screen); not modelled, so the fit keeps 46 frames off it, at most 0.63 ticks (wave 4: 8)
